A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 37 pages of v1 and 33 pages of v2, including Appendices A–C, support comparison. Figures, tables, equations and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization simulations in Figures 2 and 4 and a teacher-student neural-network experiment with five training runs in Section 2.3 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations and neural-network results. Figure 4 appears in Appendix C.2 rather than alongside the conclusion.

M1.justification: The heavy-ball ODE, Nesterov updates, decreasing-step scheme and AGNES updates are retained. Renaming the geometric assumption to the strong aiming condition and correcting the Lyapunov analysis do not change the optimization procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic teacher-student regression task and the same one- and two-dimensional optimization examples. No dataset, domain or evaluated scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 4 retains the same gradient-descent versus Nesterov comparison. The additional methods discussed in related work are not added as experimentally evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain 100 synthetic points in R12, the same teacher and student architectures, 10,000 training epochs, learning rate 0.005, momentum 0.99 and finite-difference increment 0.01. The optimization-example settings also match. Correcting the second-derivative notation does not change the stated computation.

E4.justification: The step-size-dependent trajectories, neural-network curvature analysis and parameter-dependent gradient-descent comparison in Figures 2–4 are retained. Moving Figure 4 and its discussion to Appendix C.2 does not add or remove an analysis.

E5.justification: Both report five neural-network training runs and show curves for different random initializations. There are no changes to repeated-run information, uncertainty summaries, confidence intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: All four figures retain identical plotted images. Both report final neural-network training losses between 10^-12 and 10^-9 and the same finding that gradient descent can outperform Nesterov near the illustrated parameter threshold. No empirical result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the continuous-time theorem's initial condition from f(x0)−inf f<α to f(x0)<α, matching the defined sublevel set (v1 Theorem 7; v2 Theorem 6). Appendix B.2 restores the missing √μ factor in the Lyapunov expression, and B.3 restores an expectation in the stochastic descent estimate. The principal convergence bounds and proof strategies remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims retain acceleration under weaker geometric assumptions in continuous time and deterministic/stochastic discrete time. The dedicated contribution subsection elaborates the treatment of tangential motion, whose novelty was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds the ReLU applicability limitation and explains the importance of C1,1 versus C2 smoothness for the PL/strong-aiming distinction. Appendix C.2 clarifies that Figure 4 uses parameters guaranteed over a function class. Conversely, Section 3.2 drops v1's small-μ/L qualification when describing Nesterov as much faster.

D1.justification: The architectures, training parameters and finite-difference procedures were already disclosed in v1 and remain in v2. No implementation instructions, hardware or runtime information, or code/data access resources are added or removed.

R1.justification: Sections 1.1–1.2 substantially expand positioning: v2 explicitly relates its assumption to existing quasi-strong convexity, distinguishes Hermant et al.'s deterministic, unique-minimizer setting and shared Hessian bound, and adds heavy-ball non-acceleration, KL and smoothness comparisons. Rebjock and Boumal also inform Sections 2.2–2.3. The Gupta et al. 2023-to-2024 reference change concerns the same AGNES work.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Our Contribution subsection, relocates the projection lemma to Section 3.1, expands proof explanations and consistently adopts strong aiming terminology. It also condenses the experimental description and revises the conclusion. These are targeted reorganizations within the retained main-section and appendix structure.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted into the ICLR style, changing typography, text margins, heading and header treatment, equation-number placement and caption layout. Figures are resized or repositioned, with Figure 4 moved to Appendix C.2. The plotted content and geometric-condition table structure remain.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical consistency through the initial-condition and Lyapunov-factor corrections, explains the proof construction more clearly, and better identifies prior work and applicability limits. The empirical evidence and main guarantees remain stable. The gradient-descent counterexample becomes less prominent in the appendix, and the speedup wording loses a useful qualification, but these limited drawbacks do not outweigh the corrections and clearer positioning.
